Consider the square region $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
Δ={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 1}
$$

and the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:(u,v)\to (x(u,v),y(u,v)),
$$

where 

$$
x={u}^{2}+{v}^{2},\,y=u.
$$

Find the image of $Δ$ under the action of $T.$ 

*Hint: You may assume that $T$ has no critical points in the interior of $Δ.$*
worked_solution:
We're told that $T$ has no critical points in the interior of $Δ.$ So, to map the entire region $Δ$ onto the $xy$-plane, we transform each side of $Δ$ separately:

- Consider the image of the side ${S}_{1},$ where we have $v=0$ and $0\le u\le 1.$ Substituting $v=0$ into our transformation equations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y) & =T(u,v) &  \\  & =({u}^{2}+{v}^{2},\,u) &  \\  & =({u}^{2}+{0}^{2},\,u) &  \\  & =({u}^{2},\,u), & 0\le u\le 1.\end{aligned}
$$

This is a right-opening parabola traversed from the point $(0,0)$ to the point $(1,1)$ in the $xy$-plane.

- Consider the image of the side ${S}_{2}.$ Here, we have $u=1$ and $0\le v\le 1.$ Substituting $u=1$ into our transformation equations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y) & =T(u,v) &  \\  & =({u}^{2}+{v}^{2},\,u) &  \\  & =({1}^{2}+{v}^{2},\,1) &  \\  & =(1+{v}^{2},\,1), & 0\le v\le 1.\end{aligned}
$$

This is a horizontal line segment traversed from the point $(1,1)$ to the point $(2,1)$ in the $xy$-plane.

- Consider the image of the side ${S}_{3}.$ Here, we have $v=1$ and $1\ge u\ge 0.$ Substituting $v=1$ into our transformation equations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y) & =T(u,v) &  \\  & =({u}^{2}+{v}^{2},\,u) &  \\  & =({u}^{2}+{1}^{2},\,u) &  \\  & =({u}^{2}+1,\,u), & 1\ge u\ge 0.\end{aligned}
$$

This is a right-opening parabola traversed from the point $(2,1)$ to the point $(1,0)$ in the $xy$-plane.

- Consider the image of the side ${S}_{4}.$ Here, we have $u=0$ and $1\ge v\ge 0.$ Substituting $u=0$ into our transformation equations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y) & =T(u,v) &  \\  & =({u}^{2}+{v}^{2},\,u) &  \\  & =({0}^{2}+{v}^{2},\,0) &  \\  & =({v}^{2},\,0), & 1\ge v\ge 0.\end{aligned}
$$

 
This is a horizontal line segment traversed from the point $(1,0)$ to the point $(0,0)$ in the $xy$-plane.

Drawing the images of the sides of our square, we obtain the following image of $Δ:$
